name: Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma
aliases: Upper Urinary Tract Transitional Cell Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Association of Urology (EAU) Guidelines for UTUC

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of urothelial carcinoma in the upper urinary tract
Detection of a mass or filling defect in the renal pelvis or ureter on imaging (CT urography or MR urography)
Positive urine cytology for malignant urothelial cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus imaging evidence of tumor in the upper urinary tract
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Urine cytology and ureteroscopic biopsy may aid diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible blood in urine is the most common presenting symptom.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Flank pain due to ureteral obstruction
pathognomonic.notes: Pain typically localized to the affected side.
searchTerms: flank pain due to urinary tract obstruction
pain in side from urine flow blockage

occasional.notes: May be related to tumor necrosis or infection.
Due to lymphatic or venous obstruction.

searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney disease
renal involvement leading to high blood pressure

rare.notes: Due to ectopic production of parathyroid hormone-related protein.

searchTerms: abnormal connection from ureter to other area

rare.notes: Due to brain metastases in advanced disease.
searchTerms: brain or nerve symptoms from tumor spread

laboratory: Microscopic or gross hematuria on urinalysis
Positive urine cytology for malignant urothelial cells
Elevated serum creatinine if obstructive nephropathy present
imaging: CT urography showing filling defects or masses in renal pelvis or ureter
MR urography as alternative imaging modality
genetic: Frequent mutations in FGFR3, TP53, and HRAS genes in tumor tissue
other: Cystoscopy to exclude concomitant bladder urothelial carcinoma

distinguishingFeatures: Originates from renal parenchyma rather than urothelium
Histopathology shows clear cell or other renal carcinoma subtypes
Primary tumor located in bladder rather than upper tract
Different clinical presentation with more lower urinary tract symptoms

redFlags: Persistent gross hematuria without identifiable benign cause
Rapidly progressive flank pain with signs of obstruction
Unexplained weight loss and constitutional symptoms in elderly patient
references: European Association of Urology Guidelines on Upper Urinary Tract Urothelial Carcinoma, 2023
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Bladder Cancer, Version 6.2023
Soria F, et al. Upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a comprehensive review. World J Urol. 2022
